beginner.headline: Today (Sat Oct 17): conditional for beginners. Best 6:45–10:30 AM around the 9:24 AM high (1.8 ft): wind was light at Honolulu at 6 AM (N 6 mph), but NE trades around 20 mph are forecast to fill in. Late morning conditional; from 12:30 PM not recommended. No buoy or Canoes observation this morning.
beginner.recommendation: Go early. At 6 AM Honolulu Airport read N 6 mph and Kalaeloa NE 3 mph, so the start looks lighter than last night's models (20 mph gusting upper 20s from 6 AM); NWS still has NE around 20 mph today, with Kāneʻohe already at NE 14, so expect the trades to reach Waikīkī during the morning and drift to build. The 9:24 AM high (1.8 ft) gives the most water over the reef. NWS now calls the south swell small and declining, south shore surf below average through next week; the Friday-afternoon surf zone forecast still had south-facing 3–5 ft today (exposed shores). Models put Waikīkī around 1.3 ft at 14–15 s: small, but long-period, so watch several full set cycles (10+ minutes) before committing. Water: DOH brown-water advisories reported for Laniakea and Waimea Bay (North Shore); nothing verified for Waikīkī, and the DOH list was not reachable this morning, so check water color at Canoes and toward the Kūhiō drains and Ala Wai side after the overnight showers. One student or a small group of strong adults; several students or children only while drift stays low. Your on-site read overrides this report.

water.statement: The DOH Clean Water Branch advisory list could not be opened this run, so brown-water, bacteria and sewage advisories were not read. The Star-Advertiser reports DOH brown-water advisories for Laniakea Beach and Waimea Bay Beach on the North Shore; a Hawaii News Network repost (Oct 16) also mentions bacteria advisories without naming beaches. None of these is a Waikīkī notice, but not finding one does not prove the water is clean. Check water color.
water.why: eha-cloud page blocked for this run; DOH general advisory page lists no beaches. Overnight showers were forecast mostly windward and mauka, which lowers but doesn't remove runoff risk at Waikīkī.
water.runoff: Brown, gray, cloudy or turbid water, or visible runoff: don't go in, advisory or not. DOH guidance: storm runoff can carry sewage and pathogens; stay out of affected water for 48–72 hours after rain stops.
